world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Gonzalez de Perez, Maria Stella. 2006. Aproximacion al sistema fonetico-fonologico de la lengua muisca; Constenla Umana 1984 Los fonemas del muisca.

new_statements.quote: En cuarto lugar, la posición del acento recae por lo general en la última sílaba de la palabra. En un conteo de cien palabras acentuadas no monosilábicas el resultado fue el siguiente: acentuadas en la última sílaba, 71; acentuadas en la penúltima, 13; acentuadas en la antepenúltima, 2; acentuadas tanto en la penúltima como en la última, 8; acentuadas tanto en la antepenúltima como en la última, 1; acentuadas en las tres sílabas, 5. [...] Si se considera que el "acento" no era distintivo, se explicarían con mayor facilidad varios de los hechos mencionados [...] y el predominio muy notable de la última sílaba como su receptora.
new_statements.translation: Fourth, the position of the accent falls as a rule on the last syllable of the word. In a count of one hundred accented non-monosyllabic words the result was: accented on the last syllable, 71; on the penult, 13; on the antepenult, 2; on both penult and last, 8; on both antepenult and last, 1; on all three syllables, 5. [...] If one takes the 'accent' not to have been distinctive, several of the facts mentioned are more easily explained [...] and the very marked predominance of the last syllable as its bearer.
new_statements.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo. 1984. Los fonemas del muisca. Estudios de Lingüística Chibcha 3: 65-111. San José: Universidad de Costa Rica.
new_statements.locator: §5.2 'Prominencia dentro de la palabra', pp. 104-105 (statement on p. 105; Lugo's two passages quoted on p. 104); scan pages ocr_constenla1984/
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened via its page images ocr_constenla1984/journal p. 104) and p. 105); the PDF is image-only (extracted text layer empty), so the scanned file is derived and the images are the record. On p. 105 the quoted passage is verbatim: "En cuarto lugar, la posición del acento recae por lo general en la última sílaba de la palabra. En un conteo de cien palabras acentuadas no monosilábicas el resultado fue el siguiente: acentuadas en la última sílaba, 71; acentuadas en la penúltima, 13; acentuadas en la antepenúltima, 2; acentuadas tanto en la penúltima como en la última, 8; acentuadas tanto en la antepenúltima como en la última, 1; acentuadas en las tres sílabas, 5." and, two paragraphs down, "Si…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word prominence (marked in Lugo 1619 and the Madrid confessionary by interchangeable circumflex/grave/acute signs, which Lugo says indicate a long-pronounced vowel) falls predominantly on the final syllable: excluding the unstable postposition bohotsa 'con', 70 of 84 accented polysyllables (83%) are marked final, 11 (13%) penultimate, 1 antepenultimate, 2 both. Constenla concludes the accent was probably not distinctive and hypothesises (p. 105) a gradual increase of prominence, realised as vowel lengthening, over the last three syllables, culminating on the final one; being non-distinctive, it varied with emphasis, which explains the inconsistent marking. Lugo himself (Prólogo al lector; fol. 158) only says the marked vowel is pronounced long and that he leaves the rules of accent to usage.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not treated as such. Constenla notes some words carry marks on two or three syllables (8 penult+final, 1 antepenult+final, 5 on all three of 100) and interprets this as graded prominence rising toward the final syllable rather than secondary stress. Saravia 2015 (pedagogical, p. 11) posits secondary stress on the second syllable and main stress on the last in C-V1-h-V1-C-a words (kuhubá, bohozhá).
new_statements.exceptions: Marking is very inconsistent in both sources; the same word appears accented on the final syllable at times and on the penult (exceptionally antepenult) at others; the postposition 'con' is written at least six ways (bhôhôzhâ, bhôhozhâ, bhôhozha, bhôzhâ, bhôzha, bhozhâ); the sole apparent minimal pair ayâ 'adelante' / aîa 'muy lejos' (Lugo fol. 118) is judged unreliable. Alvar 1977: 20 had instead inferred distinctive vowel quantity coinciding with the accent; Constenla argues against this. Saravia 2015: 11, 77 (course, not a description) states the opposite default (penultimate, with 1st-conjugation futures in -nga final).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('prominencia dentro de la palabra'), based on written accent marks in a 1619 printed grammar and a 17th-c. confessionary; §5.1 treats intonation separately (punctuation may reflect final/non-final intonation contours; no source describes intonation). Confidence is limited by the philological nature of the evidence.
new_statements.identity_note: Extinct language known only from colonial (1600s) missionary sources: Lugo 1619 (printed grammar), the anonymous Bogotá ms (ed. González de Pérez 1987 / Uricoechea 1871) and the Madrid ms (ed. Lucena Salmoral). Constenla's statement is a philological inference from the accent marks in Lugo 1619 and the Madrid confessionary, not from speech. Saravia 2015 (pedagogical reconstruction for the revitalisation community) posits the opposite, penultimate, rule; it is not a primary description. No dialect issue; Duit (duit1235) is a separate sister variety mentioned by Adelaar but not covered here.

sources.note: §5.2 pp. 103-106: accent marks only in Lugo 1619 and Madrid confessionary; Lugo says marked vowel is long; marking inconsistent; count of 100 accented words: 71 final, 13 penult (83% final excluding bohotsa); accent probably not distinctive; hypothesis of gradual prominence increase culminating on the final syllable. Image-only scan, scanned with tesseract (eng, 200 dpi); pp. 104-105 verified against page images.

sources.citation: Saravia, Facundo Manuel. 2015. Curso de aproximación a la lengua chibcha o muisca, Nivel I. Chía: Fundación Zaquenzipa.
sources.note: Lección 1 §3 'Acentuación' p. 11: 'El acento produce un alargamiento de la vocal acentuada y recae en la penúltima sílaba, a menos que se indique lo contrario' (uba, hyká); C-V1-h-V1-C-a words: secondary stress on 2nd syllable, main on last (kuhubá, bohozhá); Lección 10: 1st-conjugation futures in -nga stressed on last syllable; Anexo p. 77: rule 'inferida a partir de un cuidadoso estudio de la distribución de acentos en las fuentes primarias' plus comparison with Damana, Kogi, Ika, Uwa, Kuna. Pedagogical reconstruction, contradicts Constenla's count.

sources.note: Prólogo al lector: 'Solo tendrás dificultad en el acentuar, y para esto advertirás, que adonde huviere esta ^ pronunciarás largo, poniendo el acento en la misma letra adonde estuviere la tal señal'; end of pronunciation chapter (fol. ~11v): 'lo que ay que tratar de orthographia, y acento se dexa, porque fuera querer proceder en infinito'. Uses accent marks but gives no placement rule.
